stem.text: Let \( f(x) = - \left(x + 3\right)^{3} \sin{\left(\frac{1}{x + 3} \right)} - 3 \) for \( x \ne -3 \). Use the squeeze theorem to find \( \lim_{x \to -3} f(x) \), and justify your answer.

answer_key.label: The limit is -3, because \( -3 - \left|{x + 3}\right|^{3} \le f(x) \le \left|{x + 3}\right|^{3} - 3 \) for \( x \ne -3 \) and both bounds approach -3 as x approaches -3.

worked_solution.text: Multiplying by the nonnegative quantity \( \left|{x + 3}\right|^{3} \) and adding -3 gives \( -3 - \left|{x + 3}\right|^{3} \le f(x) \le \left|{x + 3}\right|^{3} - 3 \). The factor \( - \left(x + 3\right)^{3} \) can be negative, so its absolute value is used to keep the inequality true.
Both bounds are continuous, so their limits as x approaches -3 are both -3.
